structure.title: Act I · The wreck and its director
structure.text: On deck, a boatswain needs the nobles to get out of the way. Onshore, Miranda fears for the drowning passengers. Only then does Prospero explain how much of the danger has been arranged and why he brought these people to his island.

structure.title: Acts II–IV · The island in separate parties
structure.text: The survivors find themselves in groups. A young couple meet, courtiers plot, and servants discover that wine can produce its own political following. Ariel moves between groups who have sharply limited knowledge of one another.

structure.title: Act V and epilogue · Reunion and epilogue
structure.text: Prospero can stage a meeting and provide a spectacle almost at will. What he can obtain from another person once the performance ends is a different question. The epilogue finally puts a request into the hands of the audience.

people.name: Prospero and Miranda
people.role: An exiled duke and his daughter
people.text: He tells her their history just when his recovery of power seems possible. She knows him as her father. Almost everything she learns about the political past must come through a man who has reason to present his own case.

people.name: Ariel and Caliban
people.text: Ariel has been promised freedom in return for service. Caliban remembers an island that belonged to his mother. The difference matters every time Prospero explains what either of them owes him.

context.title: Teaching someone to speak
context.text: Miranda remembers the gift of language. Caliban remembers learning the language in which he can curse his rulers. Their accounts make the history of education on the island sound quite different according to who has the floor.

notice.why: Ariel can guide a person by giving him a song whose source he cannot see. A beautiful sound can express sympathy, misdirect a listener and keep a frightened traveller moving.

passages.quote: the isle is full of noises

notice.text: Notice the labour behind the spectacle.
notice.why: Prospero gets credit for wonders that require somebody else's running, singing and scene changes. Ariel keeps track of when the working day is supposed to end.

opening: Prospero has spent years on an island with his daughter, remembering the brother who stole his position and sent them out to sea. Now his enemies are sailing past, and he has learned enough magic to bring their ship within reach. He can separate them, frighten them, and arrange what they see. Shakespeare gives an injured man extraordinary control over the people who wronged him, then lets the business of settling accounts compete with his daughter's discovery of a life beyond her father.
